start.description: start date for the data point

outlierCode.description:
outlierCode: 0 or no value -- regular point
             1 -- to be ignored when returning results of value outlier analysis
             2 -- is an estimated value
             3 -- combination of 1 and 2 together

enum (0, 1, 2)

comments.description: (Optional) any comments for the data point

isEstimated.description: Denotes if the value is an actual value or an estimated value. default = null (actual value)

dataVersion.description:
Same data points can have different data version to denote priority. Default behavior in case of overlapping
data points is to pick the data point with the highest data version.
If data version is not specified, then default (avg) overlap handling is applied to the overalapping data points

statusCode.description: Customer specific status code for the data point (may be used to denote data quality)

title:
Mixin this type to store raw Timeseries data points which happen at a "point in time" -
(having only start date time and no end - e.g. Temperature reading at a given instant in time)

This type participates in the normalization process which performs data cleansing on these points. Refer to the topic
on [normalization](ts-normalization.c3doc.md) for more information.

In order for normalization process to work, there needs to be a 1-1 mapping in between a {@link TimedDataPoint} type
& {@link TimedDataHeader} type.

For the normalization process, a single TimedDataPoint type CANNOT map to multiple TimedDataHeader types.

You also must create a Timeseries field that needs to be normalized typically denoted with an annotation
@ts (@see Ann.Ts)

Refer to [Normalization Process](ts-normalization.c3doc.md) for an end to end example.

DO NOT mixin this type if you do not want to participate in the normalization process & use the base types
(e.g. TimedDataPointFields) if you would like to inherit the base fields only

In order to represent data that has a defined start & end date time, @see IntervalDataPoint

@see normalization#how-it-works
@see IntervalDataPoint
@see TimedDataHeader
name: TimedDataPoint
